Purge tracked `.env` from Git history — quick reference

WARNING: Rewriting Git history is destructive and requires force-pushing. Coordinate with your team before doing this.

Option A — git-filter-repo (recommended)

  # Install (Linux/Windows with Python/pip)
  pip install git-filter-repo

  # Make a fresh clone (recommended) so you can safely test before pushing
  git clone --mirror https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.git repo.git
  cd repo.git

  # Remove the `.env` file from all history
  git filter-repo --invert-paths --paths .env

  # Push the cleaned history back to origin
  git push origin --force --all
  git push origin --force --tags

  # Inform everyone to re-clone, or provide recovery instructions

Option B — The BFG Repo-Cleaner (simpler UI)

  # Download BFG: https://rtyley.github.io/bfg-repo-cleaner/
  # Run in a mirrored clone
  java -jar bfg.jar --delete-files .env
  # Clean git references and garbage collect
  git reflog expire --expire=now --all
  git gc --prune=now --aggressive
  git push --force

After the push, collaborators must re-clone or follow instructions to safely rebase their work.

Post-removal checklist:
  - Rotate all provider keys immediately (AlphaVantage, Finnhub, FMP, Polygon, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google/Gemini, etc.).
  - Update CI/CD variables and `.streamlit/secrets.toml` as appropriate.
  - Add a `detect-secrets` baseline and commit it.

If you'd like I can prepare a branch and pull request that does the safe repo-side changes (redaction + new example file + docs) and then outline the exact commands required locally to complete the history purge.
